pools.pool: power_economic: criminal faction in a transit hub
keyGuarantees: genCoherence note power_economic|economics: a crime-named faction above the power threshold in a transit-trade town (measured unreachable: crime factions top out at power 7)
pools.ruling: Not scoped: no line asserts calm; the transit-trade presumption has no reader (trade-route kind) and is the key's own premise.

lines.text: {faction} holds {band} of the power in {settlement}, and {settlement} is a place goods pass through; a share of what passes is moving outside the official channels, and the trade figures are therefore a floor rather than a count.
What is written down about {settlement}'s trade and what actually moves through it are two different quantities, and the difference has an owner.
{settlement} handles more goods than its records account for, which is normal for a transit town and unusually pronounced here.
{faction} is strong in {settlement} and the transit trade is clean; whatever the faction takes, it does not take it off the road.

pools.pool: power_economic: powerful criminal faction in a prosperous settlement
keyGuarantees: genCoherence note power_economic|overview: a powerful crime-named faction in a settlement the record calls prosperous (measured unreachable)
pools.ruling: Scoped: it can render under a crisis and lines 2-3 assert present wealth, which a hunger or threat crisis contradicts.

lines.text: {faction} holds {band} of the power in {settlement}, and the town's stated prosperity is gross: a meaningful share of it never reaches the tax rolls.
{settlement} is doing well, and doing well here includes arrangements the hall would rather not itemise.
{settlement} is visibly wealthy and its public accounts are modest, and both of those things are true.
{faction} is powerful in a prosperous {settlement} and takes its share in kind rather than in coin; the rolls are accurate and incomplete in different places than a stranger would guess.

keyGuarantees: genCoherence note stress_economic|economics: the settlement is under siege while its books show trade income
pools.ruling: Crisis-keyed: the note exists only under a siege, so the pool carries poolCrisis under_siege and its lines inherit it.

lines.text: {settlement} is under siege, and the trade income on its books is what the town earned before the gates shut; what it earns now is close to nothing.
{settlement}'s market still keeps its hours and has almost nothing to sell, because nothing has come in since the siege began.
The trade {settlement} is known for is not happening, and the town's accounts have not caught up with that.
What {settlement} was worth in trade is being spent down rather than earned, and the stores are the only figure that matters while the gates hold.

keyGuarantees: genCoherence note power_stress|power: the settlement is occupied while its stability text does not mention occupation
pools.ruling: Crisis-keyed on occupation; lines 1-3 deny open disorder (unrest family) and line 4 denies occupier rule.

lines.text: {settlement} is under occupation, and the stability recorded for it describes the surface: the town is quiet because it is held, which is a different fact from the town being settled.
{settlement} is orderly and the order is not the town's own, and everybody here can tell the two apart.
Nothing in {settlement} is disturbed, and nothing in {settlement} is voluntary.
{settlement} is occupied and its own hall still governs. The occupier collects and does not administer, and legitimacy here has survived the arrangement.

pools.pool: power_economic: temple economy under a secular seat
keyGuarantees: genCoherence note power_economic|power: the church controls most economic activity while a secular faction holds the seat
pools.ruling: Scoped: line 4 asserts the seat is uncontested, which a succession-family crisis contradicts.

lines.text: Economic activity in {settlement} runs through the religious houses while formal governance rests with {govFaction}; whoever holds the trade and the tithes holds more practical power than whoever holds the seat.
The seat in {settlement} decides, and the temple is what the deciding has to be arranged around.
{settlement} has an official authority and an actual one, and they meet in the market rather than in the hall.
{settlement}'s temple carries the economy and does not reach for the seat, and {govFaction} governs without contesting the arrangement.

keyGuarantees: genCoherence note historical_economic|history: a collapse older than eighty years and a boom inside sixty on the event record (measured unreachable by name)
pools.ruling: Scoped: lines 3-4 assert present comfort and surplus, which a hunger crisis contradicts; the history itself has no reader.

lines.text: {settlement}'s prosperity was rebuilt and not inherited: the town went down a generation and more ago, and came back inside the memory of people still working.
{settlement}'s books show a hard collapse older than its living memory and a recovery a good deal newer, and the town manages risk like a place that remembers the first.
{settlement} is comfortable and does not behave comfortably; the caution here is older than the money.
The generation running {settlement} did the rebuilding, and what they decide about surplus is still being decided against the collapse rather than against the present.

keyGuarantees: the record carries at least one structural violation
pools.ruling: Colour: every line restates the key (the record disagrees with itself) and asserts no calm.

lines.text: {settlement} carries an institution its structure does not support, and the mismatch is on the record rather than in dispute.
There is something in {settlement} that a town of this shape should not be able to keep, and keeping it is costing somebody.
{settlement}'s establishment is out of proportion to the town and holds anyway, because it is not the town paying for it.

keyGuarantees: the record carries at least one structural suggestion (something missing)
pools.ruling: Colour: every line restates the key and asserts no calm.

lines.text: What {settlement}'s record shows and what {settlement} would need to work as described do not quite meet, and the gap has a short list of names on it.
{settlement} functions in a way its own description does not fully account for.
A careful reader of {settlement} finds one loose end, and it is the kind that a single institution would tie off.
